text:
Lina (Support): forwarding from FastDocs — they hit a bunch of 429s during an ingest. customer says they're on the Free tier and had a spike importing PDFs. Can we do a temporary burst or exception? Their org id: fd-88a7.
Lina (Support): pasted the error they sent: 
```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
Content-Type: application/json
X-RateLimit-Limit: 120/min
X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0
X-RateLimit-Reset: 167
{"error":"rate_limit_exceeded","message":"rate limit exceeded for endpoint /v1/generate"}
```
Lina (Support): they also included the curl they used: 
```
curl -X POST "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk_live_…" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"gpt-small","input":"<batch of docs>","concurrency":8}'
```
Ajay (DevEx): thanks — couple quick Qs: what timestamp did the spike start (UTC), and roughly how many concurrent connections? also which model were they hitting?
Lina (Support): spike started ~2026-11-02T15:04:00Z, they reported 7-9 concurrent workers all doing large multi-part requests. model=gpt-small as in the curl.
Ajay (DevEx): OK. likely hitting the per-minute token QPS bucket for Free tier. two immediate things: 1) we can recommend reducing concurrency to 2-3 and add jittered backoff, 2) we can push a temporary quota bump if Sales/Finance ok.
Ajay (DevEx): repro steps for ENG to simulate:
```
# spawn 6 concurrent curl requests to mimic their load
for i in 1 2 3 4 5 6; do 
  curl -s -X POST "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate" \
    -H "Authorization: Bearer $TEST_TOKEN" \
    -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    -d '{"model":"gpt-small","input":"lorem","max_tokens":512}' &
done
wait
```
Ajay (DevEx): When you hit the limit you'll see `X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0` and subsequent requests get 429. Add `Retry-After` handling in client.
sre-bot: detected rate-limit event for org fd-88a7 — 2026-11-02T15:04:22Z — scope=tenant_minute_token. Logged as event id rl_ev_20261102_01504.
Tom (Sales): looping in — if this is an onboarding customer we can do a one-time temporary burst for 72h while they upgrade. need expected QPS and an MRR estimate. Lina — can you paste the customer tier/contact and any trial commitments?
Lina (Support): FastDocs is on Free trial, no paid commitment yet. they asked for a short burst to finish their migration (estimated 48–72h). no billing on file.
Tom (Sales): ok — propose: 72h temporary + link to self-serve upgrade. I'll approve a one-time exception up to 3x free cap, but finance needs to sign if we push beyond that. I'll cc acct-exec after this thread.
Ajay (DevEx): engineering side — if you want a safer immediate fix without touching billing: 1) throttle concurrency at client, 2) switch to batched document ingestion endpoint (it uses a different batching policy), 3) use smaller max_tokens per request. That will avoid needing a quota bump for many customers.
Lina (Support): customer asked for the fastest path — they'd prefer we enable a temporary burst. I'll ask them to pause concurrent workers while we provision.
Tom (Sales): I'll create a billing exception ticket and mark it `temp_burst / 72h`. Lina, can you capture expected QPS? Ajay — will you accept a test token to validate the bump?
Ajay (DevEx): yes — supply a short-lived test token and I'll run the repro above. also if we do the bump please add monitoring: create a one-off alert for org fd-88a7 at 80% of the new cap so we can auto-notify if they push further.
Lina (Support): quick note to eng: here's a sample 429 header from them with timestamps — please double-check we aren't hitting any other throttles (per-route or per-api-key). They included this response headers snapshot (raw):
```
Date: Tue, 02 Nov 2026 15:04:22 GMT
X-RateLimit-Limit: 120/min
X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0
X-RateLimit-Reset: 164
Retry-After: 30
```
Ajay (DevEx): thanks — looks like standard tenant-minute token bucket. If Sales approves, ops can increment tenant quota for the window. After bump we'll re-run the concurrent curl and look for no 429s.
Tom (Sales): approving on sales side for 72h up to 3x. Lina — please confirm in the billing ticket and capture card-on-file status. If no card, we mark as prospect exception and require PO/commit if they want sustained increase.
Lina (Support): creating billing ticket now — BK-5419. adding notes: "FastDocs — temp burst 72h approved by Tom (Sales). org fd-88a7. monitor and revert if abuse." tagging Ajay for validation.
Ajay (DevEx): I'll run the repro once the bump is live and report back with timestamps and results. If we still see 429s we need to look at route-level limits or whether the ingest path has an independent cap.
Tom (Sales): I'll loop in acct exec + finance if they signal they want >72h. otherwise they'll see the self-serve upgrade CTA.
Lina (Support): summary / next steps:
- Sales (Tom) approved 72h temporary quota increase (3x free cap) — Tom to create billing exception (BK-5419).
- DevEx (Ajay) will validate with test token and repro script once bump is applied.
- Support (Lina) will tell customer to reduce concurrency until we confirm bump applied, provide best-practice snippets (backoff + batch).
- ops/eng: please enable monitoring for fd-88a7 and revert at window end.
Tom (Sales): sounds good — please add me to the billing ticket. I'll follow up with an email to FastDocs once exception is active. :thumbsup:
Ajay (DevEx): will post results in this thread after tests. :mag_right:
Lina (Support): thanks everyone, marking as in-progress.
